def find_orfs(frame_seq, offset, strand):
    # frame_seq aligned so index i corresponds to offset+i in original (for + strand)
    orfs = []
    i = 0
    L = len(frame_seq)
    while i < L-2:
        codon = frame_seq[i:i+3]

            while j < L-2:
                c = frame_seq[j:j+3]
                if c in STOPS:
                    start = offset+i
                    end = offset+j+2
                    length = end-start+1
                    orfs.append((start, end, length, strand))
                    i = j+3
                    break
                j += 3
            else:
                # ran to end, no stop
                start=offset+i; end=offset+L-1; length=end-start+1
                orfs.append((start,end,length,strand))
                i = j
                break
        else:
            i += 3
    return orfs

The file holds a single 3,000 bp DNA contig (header >region_004), no ambiguous
bases. Summary of notable features (coordinates are 1-based, inclusive):

1. DOMINANT FEATURE — one very large open reading frame (candidate gene)
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   A single uninterrupted ORF spans positions 158–2854 on the + strand,
   length 2,697 bp = 899 codons (899 aa). It begins with ATG (158–160) and
   ends at an in-frame stop codon TAA/TAG/TGA at 2852–2854.
   * Zero in-frame stop codons anywhere inside it. For a random DNA sequence
     the chance of 899 codons with no stop is ~ (61/64)^899 ≈ 1e-18, so this
     is almost certainly a genuine protein-coding gene, not chance.
   * A Shine-Dalgarno-like ribosome-binding motif GGAGG sits at 144–148,
     9–10 nt upstream of the start ATG (typical spacing).
   * Codon bias: GC at synonymous (3rd) positions = 0.59, slightly above the
     regional average (0.52); most-used codons CTG, GTG, GCG, ATT.

2. OVERLAPPING ANTISENSE ORF
   -------------------------
   A second ORF is present on the - strand, coordinates 1735–2253
   (i.e. read right-to-left in + coordinates), 519 bp = 173 aa. It lies
   entirely INSIDE the big + strand gene, an overlapping/antisense arrangement
   (start ATG at 2253, stop at 1735). No clear Shine-Dalgarno upstream of it.
   Whether this is a real second gene or a coincidental ORF is uncertain, but
   antisense overlaps are biologically interesting (often regulatory).

3. COMPOSITION
   -----------
   Length 3000 bp; A=697 C=709 G=853 T=741; GC = 52.1% (fairly uniform:
   per-200 bp windows range 46.5–58.0%). GC skew (C−G)/(C+G) is consistently
   slightly NEGATIVE across the whole fragment (C slightly exceeds G in every
   window, min ≈ −0.21 near position 1800). No skew sign-change, so no
   replication-origin transition is captured here.

4. REPEATS
   -------
   No long duplicated segments: the longest EXACT repeated substring is <15 bp,
   so no segmental duplication. Only short (≈10 bp) oligos recur, all inside
   coding sequence and most likely coincidental (e.g. GTGGTGGGTA @421 & 2518;
   CGCTGTTTGC @1110 & 1992; ACGCCGGAAA @1142 & 2540; CGCTGGCCAG @1452 & 2721).
   A short near-tandem repeat of ~11 bp occurs around 2550–2605
   (CGCAAACGCT…GCAAACGCT, ~45 bp apart).

5. REGULATORY STRUCTURES
   ---------------------
   No canonical −35/−10 promoter pair (TTGACA…TATAAT, 15–21 nt spacing) was
   found anywhere in the fragment, and no clear rho-independent terminator
   (stem-loop + T-stretch) was detected in the downstream tail (2855–3000).
   This is consistent with the 3 kb window capturing a complete gene BODY
   (start codon + RBS are present at 158) while its promoter and terminator
   lie just outside the captured region.

BOTTOM LINE
   ---------
   The region is dominated by one long, intact protein-coding ORF (158–2854,
   899 aa) with a probable RBS (GGAGG @144–148), plus an overlapping 173-aa
   antisense ORF (1735–2253). Flanking ~157 bp upstream and ~146 bp downstream
   are non-coding. Nothing highly unusual (no long repeats, no obvious mobile
   elements, no strong skew shift); the most notable property is that the
   fragment is essentially a single large gene.
"""

with open('scratch/region_004_report.txt','w') as f:
    f.write(report)
print(report)
